feed.title: Cholera Tracker: Global
feed.subtitle: Independent, sourced tracker of cholera worldwide in 2026: WHO case and death counts, countries reporting cases, how this year compares with 2025, WHO's risk level and a dated timeline.

entry.title: WHO: 275,284 cases and 2,601 deaths in 28 countries
entry.summary: WHO's August update, now published in its Weekly Epidemiological Record, covers 1 January to 30 August: 43% fewer cases and 58% fewer deaths than a year earlier. August's 41,915 new cases were 25% fewer than July's. Nigeria (69,263) and DR Congo (44,773) report the most cases in Africa.
entry.content:
WHO's August update, now published in its Weekly Epidemiological Record, covers 1 January to 30 August: 43% fewer cases and 58% fewer deaths than a year earlier. August's 41,915 new cases were 25% fewer than July's. Nigeria (69,263) and DR Congo (44,773) report the most cases in Africa.

Sources: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record (2 Oct)

entry.title: WHO: 2025 had the most cholera deaths since 1999
entry.summary: 47 countries reported 451,499 cases and 7,870 deaths to WHO in 2025. Deaths rose 30% although fewer cases were reported, and seven countries accounted for about 90% of cases and deaths. WHO says the true burden is substantially higher.
entry.content:
47 countries reported 451,499 cases and 7,870 deaths to WHO in 2025. Deaths rose 30% although fewer cases were reported, and seven countries accounted for about 90% of cases and deaths. WHO says the true burden is substantially higher.

Sources: WHO, Down To Earth, The Guardian Nigeria

entry.title: ECDC: 249,136 cases worldwide this year
entry.summary: ECDC's monthly overview counts 249,136 cases, including 1,970 deaths, from 1 January to 28 September, against 436,268 cases and 4,449 deaths at the same point in 2025. In the month to 28 September it recorded 46,153 new cases and 140 deaths; Afghanistan (34,378), DR Congo (8,505) and Yemen (1,885) reported the most cases. ECDC's totals are a separate count from the WHO figures above.

entry.title: Afghanistan's acute watery diarrhoea cases fall in August
entry.summary: WHO reports 18,329 cases of acute watery diarrhoea with dehydration and 4 deaths in August, 23.6% fewer cases than July's 23,985. Afghanistan has recorded 102,469 such cases this year.

entry.title: UNICEF: cholera is spreading across borders in West and Central Africa
entry.summary: UNICEF says outbreaks are accelerating in six countries: DR Congo, the Republic of the Congo, Nigeria, Chad, Cameroon and the Central African Republic. It reports more than 50,000 cases and 338 deaths in Nigeria this year, and more than 30,400 cases and nearly 700 deaths in DR Congo. The same strain is circulating in Chad, Cameroon and Nigeria around Lake Chad. UNICEF asks for $15 million for the next six months.

entry.title: WHO: May cases up 43%; global risk very high
entry.summary: WHO counts 114,829 cases and 1,318 deaths in 23 countries from 1 January to 31 May, including 29,610 new cases in May. It rates the global risk very high, with about 1 billion people at risk.
entry.content:

entry.title: WHO's global cholera reports become monthly updates
entry.summary: After 32 external situation reports, WHO's reports on the multi-country cholera situation continue in 2026 as monthly epidemiological updates.
entry.content:
